name: The Nore
status: trial: a first config to prove the thames_793 source on the estuary (no port, a tide, the sea); the anchors are placeholders until the chain places them
about: The Thames mouth c. 800: the Nore, Sheppey's north shore and the Medway's mouth, at true size
centre_about: British National Grid: Sheerness at the Medway's mouth, Grain to the west, the Nore anchorage to the north-east

rivers.name: Thames estuary and Medway
rivers.about: thames_793's class 3: the estuary's channel (EMODnet's bed, datum-corrected, in the raster) and the Medway; the carve only makes the shallows at least 4 m under the mean level, the raster's bed kept where deeper

tide.about: High water +1.25 m ODN (thames_793.py's HW_793, the level the raster's marsh is set to down the whole estuary); the mean range 4.0 m from Research/water_levels/north_sea_core.json thames_estuary_outer (c. 800 about today's at the mouth, an estimate). Low water = high water - range.

outer.about: the EA LIDAR Composite DTM 2022 of today, 70 m median

sea.about: EMODnet DTM 2024 under the 800 water where the raster has nothing, its chart datum (LAT) moved to ODN by thames_793.py's LAT_ODN table

channel.name: Thames estuary
channel.about: GRWL has no centre line in the open estuary: the deep-water path between the two ends

cover_names.1: dry ground by the water: the low cliffs' and knolls' tops (fields, hay, sheep)
cover_names.7: London clay hills: dry old high ground (fields, oak and hazel on the driest parts)

anchors.heading: auto
anchors.about: up the Thames toward Lundenwic (a placeholder)

anchors.heading: auto
anchors.about: out to the North Sea past the Nore (a placeholder)
